title: Judea & Samaria Desk
subtitle: The Palestinian Authority, security, settlement and land in Judea and Samaria

items.headline: Heavy, prolonged gunfire from Kafr Qadum heard in Kedumim
items.summary: On the evening of 8 October residents of Kedumim, in Samaria, heard prolonged heavy gunfire from the Arab village of Kafr Qadum, a few hundred metres away, and the security department called out the community’s forces and the IDF. The head of the Kedumim council, Uziel Vatik, said that so many weapons so close to a Jewish community cannot be accepted, whether the shooting was a clan quarrel or something else. He demanded that the army enter Kafr Qadum in force to collect the weapons and arrest terrorists.

items.headline: Authority security men sent to the olive harvest in civilian clothes
items.summary: Hakol Hayehudi reported that the Palestinian Authority regularly sends members of its security forces, often in civilian clothes, to olive harvests in Area C and next to Jewish communities, under the name of “protection from settlers”; the director-general of the Palestinian police, Major-General Alam al-Saqa, has ordered higher readiness for the season. The practice goes back to a decision of Prime Minister Salam Fayyad in 2011 and to a later framework called “harvest in the hot zones”, which sends officers and intelligence men to points of friction. The report followed the death at Burqa of Ali al-Bazari, an officer of the National Security Forces, in a clash with the IDF after a Jewish shepherd was attacked.

items.headline: Attacks on shepherds in Binyamin rise sharply; farmers receive body cameras
items.summary: The Binyamin Regional Council has begun to give body cameras to farmers after a sharp rise in incidents at the start of the olive harvest. By the council’s figures, reports of incidents near farms rose from about 23 to about 48 in the first week of the harvest, attacks on shepherds rose from three to eleven, and more than 140 attacks on shepherds have been recorded since the start of the year. The council head and Yesha Council chairman, Yisrael Gantz, said the cameras would let the world see what actually happens on the ground.

items.headline: New community of Goder in the northern Jordan Valley to be inaugurated on 14 October
items.summary: The new community of Goder, in the northern Jordan Valley, will be formally inaugurated on Wednesday, 14 October. Twelve families already live there, the first of whom arrived about two months ago, and 400 more housing units are planned. The cabinet approved the community on Jerusalem Day 2025; it stands on the site of a former paratrooper base at a junction on Route 5799 between Tubas and Maskiyot.

items.headline: First tent put up again at Netzach Shmuel after the demolition
items.summary: After the Civil Administration and the Border Police demolished the hilltop community of Netzach Shmuel, near Adei Ad in Binyamin, the young men who live there returned to the same hill. They have put up the first tent again.

items.letter: Added to the desk on 9 October from +972 Magazine
items.headline: Seventeen settlements approved in the Jenin district since early 2025
items.summary: According to figures from Peace Now cited by +972 Magazine, the government has approved 17 settlements in the Jenin district since the start of 2025, among them four evacuated in 2005; Ganim and Kadim have now been re-established, and Defence Minister Katz spoke at the ceremony for Ganim on 13 August. The army has set up six new camps across the district, one of them inside the city of Jenin, and another is planned. In July the commander of Central Command, Major General Avi Bluth, signed at least 15 orders taking about 200 dunams in Areas A and C for a road between the new settlements of Emek Dotan and Noa; Peace Now says this is the first use of such orders in Area A for the needs of settlement since the Oslo Accords.

items.headline: Katz: what was done in Gaza and Lebanon will come to Judea and Samaria
items.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz said this week that the IDF is preparing as never before for a “turning of the barrels”, in which the forces of the Palestinian Authority would turn their weapons on Israelis. “If anyone dares to turn weapons against us, what we did in Gaza and Lebanon will come to Judea and Samaria,” he said, adding that Israel would answer with an all-out campaign. Dr. Edy Cohen told Channel 14 that the threat is “not science fiction”, recalled that such forces turned on their hosts in Jordan, Lebanon and Kuwait, and criticised the security cabinet for not yet deciding on Minister Ben Gvir’s call to dismantle the Authority.

items.headline: Stones near Yitzhar and a firebomb at a bus from al-Fawwar
items.summary: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria reported that at 20:11 on 7 October Arabs threw stones at vehicles between the Yitzhar interchange and the small Yitzhar junction. At 20:42 Arabs from al-Fawwar, in the Hebron hills, threw a firebomb at a bus; it burned at the side of the road. No one was hurt in either attack.
items.source: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria, via Yisrael Medad (X)

items.headline: Nine Jews detained near Susya and Sinia; residents report police violence
items.summary: The police said that Border Police detained seven suspects near Susya, in the southern Hebron hills, over what they called extreme violence, and two residents of Samaria after a reported assault near the village of Sinia. The legal-aid group Honenu gave a different account: six people were detained during the evacuation of an outpost near Susya, and residents described severe violence by officers and heavy fire of rubber bullets. Several residents were hurt.

items.headline: Broad arrests for incitement and for support of the 7 October massacre
items.summary: Alongside the demolition of the house of the murderer of Netanel Shukron, forces of the IDF, the Shin Bet and the police opened broad brigade operations across Judea and Samaria. Dozens of wanted men who had publicly supported the massacre of 7 October were arrested, together with men identified with Hamas, and thorough searches for weapons were made. The IDF said that it will continue to act on its own initiative against terror infrastructure.

items.headline: Groner: the Authority is heavily armed, and its workers build Israel’s defences
items.summary: Marking three years since the massacre, the journalist Elchanan Groner wrote that the next great attack could come at any moment from armed Arab citizens of Israel and from the Palestinian Authority, which he described as armed to the neck, including with armoured vehicles. He wrote that IDF bases, community fences, armouries and security cameras are built by workers from the Authority, and that convoys of smugglers cross every day from the Hebron hills to Arad. He also noted that the IDF had not explained the release of the smuggler whose vehicle rammed an IDF Humvee on 5 October.

items.headline: Officer of the Authority’s forces killed in attack on a shepherd near Sebastia
items.summary: On 7 October Arabs from Ramin and Burqa attacked a shepherd of about twenty from the Brit Avraham farm near the old railway station at Sebastia; a stone or concrete block struck his head, and he now has a severe head injury, and four others who came to help were lightly hurt. The IDF said that a commander shot a man running at him with a suspicious object. Arab channels named the dead man as Ali Hussein of Bazariya, an officer of the Palestinian Authority security forces, whom Elchanan Groner described as a soldier of the National Security Forces.

items.headline: Shepherds attacked at Givat Tidhar and Anatot; explosive device found near Burqa
items.summary: A shepherd from Givat Tidhar was wounded by Arabs from Deir Abu Mash'al who had presented themselves as olive pickers, and about eight Arabs with clubs and stones attacked shepherds from a farm near Anatot, injuring one in the head. During the night Arabs from Burqa placed a flag of the PLO and an explosive device made of a gas cylinder and a battery on an access road; a sapper destroyed it in the morning. Attackers from al-Mughayyir again spread poisoned bait near the Allon Road, and a goat died.

items.headline: IDF demolishes monuments to terrorists and the house of the Ein Ria murderer
items.summary: IDF forces began a broad operation to demolish dozens of monuments glorifying terrorists, among them a central monument in Nablus and one in Ya'bad to a man convicted in the murder of Avner Maimon in 2003. Notices left for residents said that anyone who glorifies terror will be arrested for incitement. On the same day the IDF demolished the house of Qadri Samara, who murdered Netanel Shukron of Alei Zahav at the Ein Ria spring.

items.headline: Ben Gvir: the Palestinian Authority must be brought down
items.summary: Speaking beside the separation fence near Road 6, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said that hostile elements are training and arming themselves behind the fence, and that kidnapping, terror or a “turning of the barrels” could reach the centre of the country. He said that he is the only member of the security cabinet who votes to bring the Authority down, while decisions to strengthen it come before the cabinet month after month. He said that Israel must take the initiative against the Authority as it did in Gaza.

items.headline: American state legislators visit Eival and the new communities of northern Samaria
items.summary: A bipartisan delegation of state legislators from Florida, Illinois, Texas, Indiana, Missouri and Alabama visited northern Samaria as guests of Yossi Dagan, head of the Samaria Regional Council. They saw Peduel, the new community of Eival founded this summer, the altar of Joshua on Mount Eival and the lookout above Joseph’s Tomb. The members are expected to promote state laws requiring the name “Judea and Samaria” in official documents and laws against boycotts of its businesses.

items.headline: Arab crime organisations hold military weapons, warns head of government task force
items.summary: Roy Kahlon, head of the Prime Minister’s Office task force against crime in the Arab sector, said that Arab crime organisations inside Israel now hold LAW anti-tank rockets, MAG machine guns, Claymore-type charges and explosive drones. He described a wartime scenario in which armed groups in vehicles with Israeli plates block roads, strike infrastructure and fire in residential areas. He compared the present approach to the assumptions held about Hamas before 7 October.

items.headline: Katz sets out plan for war if the Authority’s forces turn on Israel
items.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz told the cabinet that, beyond an attempt by terror groups to repeat 7 October, the security establishment is preparing for a complete reversal by the Palestinian Authority’s forces and the Tanzim militias. He said that this would mean an all-out war against the Authority, not another wave of terror. An operational plan approved by Prime Minister Netanyahu and Mr. Katz provides for a short and intense campaign with air and ground fire, the targeting of senior figures, the destruction of weapons caches and the large-scale evacuation of Arab residents from combat zones.

items.headline: Mass poisoning of a flock near the Allon Road
items.summary: Nine sheep and a sheepdog died, and more than forty sheep were harmed, after poison was poured into a water trough on a hilltop near the Allon Road in Binyamin. Residents said that the cell came from the direction of al-Mughayyir; the suspects have not been caught. Residents described it as the thirteenth poisoning of pastures along the Allon Road in the past year.

items.headline: Shin Bet chief warns of military-type organisation among the Negev Bedouin
items.summary: David Zini, head of the Shin Bet, told the security cabinet of “very worrying” organisation in the unrecognised Bedouin settlements of the Negev, including infrastructure of a military character. He said that attempts have been identified to set up frameworks resembling military battalions. He also warned of ties between residents and terror organisations, Hamas among them.

items.headline: Central Command adopts the doctrine of “the community as a fortress”
items.summary: The IDF stated that Central Command has adopted the doctrine of “the community as a fortress”, with more observation, intelligence, weapons and security components inside the communities, and that all army camps in Judea and Samaria are being turned into fortified posts. Its forces continue to hold the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps under Operation Iron Wall. On the eastern border, Division 96, “Gilad”, has been established with five territorial rapid-response “David brigades”.

items.headline: Orders signed to demolish monuments glorifying terrorists
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reported that the IDF appears to be changing its policy on monuments glorifying terrorists, which until now required separate legal and command approval for each demolition. Orders signed by Brigadier General Kobi Heller, commander of the Judea and Samaria Division, have been distributed, and IDF sources said that an orderly procedure now allows demolitions as part of brigade operations. Arab media published one such order, placed on a monument in the Jenin area.

items.headline: Smuggler whose vehicle rammed an IDF Humvee is released
items.summary: Mahmoud Daisat, a known smuggler of illegal residents, was released on 6 October and handed to the Red Crescent as a free man. He had driven the vehicle that rammed an IDF Humvee in the Hebron hills on 5 October. Security officials expressed strong anger at the release and described the daily convoys of smugglers between the Hebron hills and the Negev as a serious danger; the IDF Spokesperson said that an inquiry has been opened.

items.headline: A new community, Elisha, to be established near Jericho
items.summary: Residents of Beit Hogla, in the Jordan Valley, are moving on to establish a new community named Elisha on the outskirts of Jericho. Azriel Pikar, one of the four founding families of Beit Hogla almost eleven years ago, said that Beit Hogla now has about sixty families. He said that the cranes for Elisha are being raised in daylight, with the support of all the authorities and the approval of the government.

items.headline: Homes demolished at Ora Israel and Netzach Shmuel
items.summary: Border Police and Civil Administration inspectors in large numbers demolished four family homes at two settlement points, Ora Israel near Salfit and Netzach Shmuel near Adei Ad, and confiscated the flock of Ora Israel. Several teenagers were hurt by police and five were arrested. Residents describe Ora Israel as a barrier to Authority control of the Area A bloc between Salfit and Ramallah.

items.headline: Kfar Ana: drone footage shows Palestinians started the fire blamed on settlers
items.summary: Palestinians from Ein Yabrud set fire to a roadblock of tyres on the access road to Kfar Ana, between Beit El and Ofra, and the fire spread to a nearby Palestinian car lot. The village then said that settlers had set the lot alight. Drone footage shows the Palestinians beside the fire, and the IDF said that its trackers determined from the evidence that Palestinians had set it.

items.headline: Smotrich petitions the High Court to advance the E1 tender
items.summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich filed an urgent petition against an instruction by Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to delay the opening of bids in the tender for 1,234 housing units in E1, at seven sites in the Mevaseret Adumim neighbourhood of Ma'ale Adumim. He said that political approval was given in October 2025, before the election period. He said that the building will connect Jerusalem and Ma'ale Adumim for the first time and decide whether there is continuous Israeli territory.

items.headline: Children’s bus stoned on the Gilad road; poison spread on two pastures
items.summary: Arabs stoned a bus carrying children on the Gilad road in Samaria, the second attack on that road in two days. Attackers from Abu Falah spread poison on pastures near the Allon Road, and five sheep fell severely ill. Near Ma'ale Amos, in Gush Etzion, residents found dates laced with poison spread on their pastures by attackers from Kisan.

items.headline: Shin Bet chief raises the return of administrative detention against Jews
items.summary: David Zini, head of the Shin Bet, told the security cabinet that he may demand the return of administrative detention, imprisonment without charge or trial, against Jews in Judea and Samaria. Defence Minister Katz ended the use of such orders against Jews in November 2024, and any return rests with him. Coalition members of Knesset criticised the remarks, and Tally Gottlieb called on Mr. Zini to resign.

items.headline: Second attacker in the Hanina Farm stabbing attempt arrested
items.summary: The IDF announced that, after a joint pursuit under Shin Bet guidance, it arrested the second terrorist in the attempted stabbing near Kafr Rammun, together with a further suspect. Residents of the farm said that the first attacker set a vehicle alight and ran at them with a knife. One resident stopped him with his vehicle, and no Israelis were hurt.

items.headline: Two attempted attacks in Binyamin and the Hebron hills
items.summary: A terrorist with a knife came to the grazing land of Hanina Farm near Rammun, set fire to an Israeli vehicle and tried to stab residents, who stopped him with their vehicle. Earlier, near Bani Na'im east of Hebron, a vehicle carrying three Palestinians struck an IDF vehicle, and the soldiers fired. One occupant was killed and two were wounded; no soldiers or civilians were hurt.

items.headline: Minister Strook confronts the Shin Bet chief in the security cabinet
items.summary: Minister Orit Strook told the security cabinet that the security services give a partial picture of violence in Judea and Samaria, and that Palestinians attack shepherds and endanger their lives. Shin Bet head David Zini replied that Palestinians do not burn Jewish homes. Member of Knesset Limor Son Har-Melech answered with a photograph of the fire at Havat Gilad and asked whether Mr. Zini had dealt with the threat from the Palestinian security services.

items.headline: Authority forces warned before IDF raids, and the targets appeared on Islamic Jihad channels
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that before an overnight operation in northern Samaria the IDF told the Palestinian Authority security services in advance, so that they would withdraw from the area. The targets of the operation then appeared on Telegram channels of Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Those channels later complained that the IDF had entered Meithalun without warning, unlike the fourteen other targets.

items.headline: Central Command presents plans for a “turning of the barrels” to the cabinet
items.summary: The defence establishment was to present to the security cabinet the plans of Central Command for a scenario in which the weapons of the Palestinian Authority security services are turned against IDF forces or Israeli communities. On 7 September Defence Minister Katz said that he and the Prime Minister had instructed the IDF to prepare for a full war against the Authority’s senior figures and security services if they opened an attack of the 7 October type.

items.headline: Border Police prepare to demolish settlement points
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that Border Police carried out preparatory patrols for demolitions at no fewer than four settlement points, some of which house families. He criticised Brigadier General Kobi Heller for turning his forces against the settlements instead of against the organisers of disturbances during the olive harvest.

items.headline: Feiglin rejects the claim that armed settlers enter Arab villages to kill
items.summary: Moshe Feiglin, chairman of Zehut, challenged Gadi Eisenkot to give one name of an Arab whom a settler had deliberately gone to his village and murdered in the last ten years. He said that the Arabs killed in such incidents were terrorists who infiltrated communities and were stopped by the security forces or the emergency squads. He called Mr. Eisenkot’s account a gross lie and incitement.

items.headline: Hilltop communities seek recognition by the state, including in Areas A and B
items.summary: Residents of the new hilltop communities are campaigning before the elections for recognition and regularisation, including for communities in Areas A and B and on land registered as private. Shalhevet Goldstein of Givat Maoz Esther proposed cancelling the Oslo Accords, a new registration of all land, and the definition of a hilltop community as a security component that may be placed in Area B.

items.headline: Overnight raids in fourteen towns, and a general closure for 5 and 7 October
items.summary: Israeli forces raided at least fourteen villages and towns, arrested dozens of wanted men, and broke up a cell in Araneh, near Nablus, that was in advanced planning for an attack. In Awarta forces secured worshippers at the tombs of Eleazar and Ithamar. Defence Minister Katz ordered a general closure on Judea and Samaria on 5 and 7 October.

items.headline: False report of settler violence at Sebastia
items.summary: The main Nablus Telegram channel reported that settlers were attacking residents in Iyarib, Sebastia. Elisha Yered wrote after watching the video that the claim is false, and that footage presented as such an attack shows Jewish youths practising self-defence at the edge of a community.

items.headline: Molotov attack on Eretz HaTzvi farm stopped by the owner
items.summary: Two attackers carrying Molotov cocktails came to Eretz HaTzvi farm near Nachliel, in western Binyamin, intending to set it on fire. The owner followed the arrest procedure, then fired and wounded one; no Israelis were hurt. The Palestinian Authority Health Ministry and WAFA presented the death of a 19-year-old from Kafr Aqab as a killing by settlers near Kobar.

items.headline: Four foreign activists face removal after olive-harvest provocations
items.summary: Four foreign activists who took part in a violent olive-harvest provocation in Gush Kana, in which Jewish youths were hurt, were detained by the IDF near Tapuah. They were questioned at the Ariel police station, and their file was sent to the Population and Immigration Authority for a hearing on removal from Israel. Yossi Dagan said that those who come to provoke must know that there is a price.

items.headline: Wave of attacks in Samaria under cover of the olive harvest
items.summary: Near Nahal Kane and Tzon Aviezer, Arabs from Asira al-Qibliya attacked Jews and a Jewish youth was wounded in the head by a stone. Near Avnei Elad about fifty Arabs attacked settlers with stones, and Nahal Battalion 50 arrested five. Rioters from al-Mughayyir threw stones at a shepherd from Givat Or Nachman, and the IDF arrested two.

items.headline: Fatah and the anti-settlement committee prepare harvest riots in Binyamin
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that Fatah and the Committee Against Settlements held a long preparatory meeting in the Ramallah district with village Fatah secretaries. The meeting was held ahead of planned olive-harvest riots in Binyamin.

items.headline: About fifty terror suspects arrested during Sukkot
items.summary: During Sukkot the IDF, with Battalion 931 and the Maglan unit under the Samaria Brigade, arrested about fifty terror suspects, among them a Hamas activist in Nablus. Forces seized weapons, drones and materials for explosive devices, and struck a terrorist who tried to throw a charge at them.

items.headline: Stone attack near Yasuf, and an attempt to drag a youth into the village
items.summary: Dozens of Palestinians threw stones at a group of Israelis at a water cistern by the Anton farm, between Tapuach and Rechelim; police said a boy of about fourteen was lightly wounded and are examining a claim that attackers tried to drag one of the group toward the village. An armed security man stopped the attempt, and troops fired to disperse the rioters. Palestinian officials and several foreign outlets later presented the same afternoon as a killing by settlers.

items.headline: Shepherd stoned by rioters from al-Mughayyir
items.summary: Dozens of rioters from al-Mughayyir, in Binyamin, attacked a Jewish shepherd from a nearby outpost with stones; he was not hurt. Witnesses said that the IDF response was weak, and that the village has grown more aggressive since the Paratroopers replaced the Duchifat Battalion in that sector.

items.headline: Olive pickers attack Beit Karnaim farm and try to seize the owner’s weapon
items.summary: Three Palestinians picking olives refused to leave the grazing land of Beit Karnaim farm near Maoz Tzur and threw stones at residents, wounding one in the head. They tried to seize the farm owner’s weapon, and he fired three shots into the air; one attacker was detained. The Binyamin Regional Council said that the harvest must not be used as cover for attacks.

items.headline: Dummy charge wrapped in a Hamas flag closes Route 463
items.summary: An object that looked like an explosive charge, wrapped in a Hamas flag, was placed on Route 463, the Wallerstein Road in Binyamin. The road was closed for about two hours until checks showed that it was a dummy.

items.headline: Warning that the Authority’s anti-settlement committee will use the olive harvest for attacks
items.summary: Elisha Yered wrote that the Arab olive harvest would open on 2 October and would be used for attacks near Jewish communities. He asked the commander of Central Command and the commander of the Judea and Samaria police district to arrest Mu'id Sha'aban and his group from the Palestinian Authority committee for fighting the settlements. This was a request, not a report of an arrest.

items.headline: Shepherd attacked near Maoz Tzur by about fifty masked men
items.summary: Four men attacked a Jewish shepherd at a farm near Maoz Tzur, and about fifty masked men from Beit Ur al-Tahta then joined them with clubs, stones and tear gas. Two Jews were hurt, and about one hundred metal spikes were found on an access road. About ninety minutes later some twenty men stoned a shepherd from the Metzudat David farm near al-Mughayyir.

items.headline: New settlement point, Golot, established near Otniel
items.summary: A new settlement point named Golot has been established in the Hebron hills, a few kilometres from Otniel, near the springs and Tel Devir. A road has been prepared, a metal structure placed, and a guard kept there day and night for two to three weeks. A group of families from Otniel and Tekoa is waiting to move in.

items.headline: Prayer at Beitunia square after the kidnapping of a reservist by Palestinian police
items.summary: Hundreds of residents of western Binyamin came in more than 80 vehicles to Beitunia square for morning prayers under IDF security. The organisers said it was a response to the kidnapping, about a month earlier and nearby, of an IDF reservist by terrorists from the Palestinian police. They called on the IDF and the government to restore control and security in the area.

items.headline: Thousands pray at Joseph’s Tomb with the Four Species
items.summary: Thousands entered Joseph’s Tomb in Nablus in two rounds with IDF approval, for the first mass morning prayer there with the Four Species in several decades. Senior commanders, members of Knesset and Yossi Dagan attended. Mr. Dagan and Zvi Sukkot called for the full return of the Od Yosef Chai yeshiva to the tomb.

items.headline: Attacks on Israelis under cover of the olive harvest in Samaria and Binyamin
items.summary: Olam Katan reported that on the morning of 9 October Arabs from Zeita waited in an olive grove in the Gush Kana area, between Yitzhar and Emanuel, and stoned the car of Israeli hikers; the windscreen was damaged and no one was hurt. The same morning a Samaria resident on an all-terrain vehicle was rammed and lightly injured near Tapuah, and a Jew was lightly injured in the face by stones near Jama'in, south of Nablus. In the afternoon Elisha Yered reported stone-throwing near Gilad Farm and a booby-trapped PLO flag on the grazing land of the Hesed L'Avraham farm on Mount Hazor, and he warned that dozens of attacks were to be expected over the Sabbath.

items.headline: Hikers remove a monument to the murderer of Rabbi Nehemia Lavi and Aharon Bennett
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that hikers of the Chargavim group, touring western Binyamin on 9 October, found a monument in Surda to Muhannad Halabi, who murdered Rabbi Nehemia Lavi and Aharon Bennett in Jerusalem in October 2015, and removed it. Ynet, citing local Palestinian sources, described the same events as an attack by armed settlers who threw stones, fired in the air and damaged a monument. The episode came in the same week that the IDF demolished dozens of monuments to terrorists in Nablus, Jenin and nearby villages.

items.headline: Katz orders removal of far-left activists; Jonathan Pollak detained near Tapuah
items.summary: Hityashvut Achshav reported on 8 October that Defence Minister Israel Katz had directed that administrative removal orders be issued against far-left activists, including foreign nationals, who come to Judea and Samaria to provoke clashes with Israeli residents. The directive followed a request by Yisrael Gantz, chairman of the Yesha Council, on behalf of all the local council heads. On the morning of 9 October soldiers detained the Israeli anarchist Jonathan Pollak and the activist Roman Levin near Kfar Tapuah for violating a closed military zone order, according to JFeed.

items.headline: Hundreds walk the Wallerstein Road and call for it to be reopened to Israelis
items.summary: Hityashvut Achshav reported that on the morning of 9 October hundreds of hikers and residents, organised by the Chargavim group, walked from Beit El to Dolev along the Wallerstein Road, which has been closed to Israeli traffic for about 26 years, and held what the report called the first prayer on the road in 30 years. They called for full security and civil control of the road and for it to be reopened, which would cut the journey from Beit El to western Binyamin from about an hour to ten minutes. The organisers said the walk was the first step of a wider campaign.

items.headline: A further seizure order in Area A inside the city of Jenin
items.summary: WAFA's Hebrew service reported on 6 October, citing the Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, that the IDF has issued seizure order No. 33/26 for 741 square metres in the al-Jabriyat neighbourhood of Jenin, in Area A. The order was signed on 5 October as immediate and urgent on grounds of military need, is valid for 60 days, and covers a narrow strip along a road route. It adjoins and partly overlaps an earlier order of 7 May 2026 for 7.247 dunams and extends the seized corridor eastward.

items.headline: Paving begins on the Homesh–Sa-Nur road in northern Samaria
items.summary: Arutz 7 reported on 6 October that, after six months of earthworks, paving had begun on the new road between Homesh and Sa-Nur, which bypasses the Palestinian village of Silat al-Dhahr. The road is meant to give safe, continuous travel between the re-established communities of northern Samaria. The head of the Samaria Regional Council, Yossi Dagan, said that eight communities have already been established in northern Samaria and that eleven more are to follow, nineteen in place of the four evacuated in 2005.

items.headline: First Sabbath of the olive harvest: a youth from Givat Tidhar is struck on the head
items.summary: On 10 October hundreds of Arabs from Deir Abu Mash'al, with foreign and far-left activists, some of them masked and carrying clubs, came up towards Givat Tidhar in Wadi Zarqa, western Binyamin, under the pretext of picking olives. Residents held back the crowd until the troops arrived; a youth from the hilltop was struck on the head and taken to Assaf Harofeh hospital, conscious. The Palestinian Red Crescent said nine Palestinians were injured at Deir Abu Mash'al, and four masked foreign activists taken to the Modi'in Illit police station elsewhere were later released without explanation.

items.headline: Twenty-three attacks on Israelis in two days, most under cover of the harvest
items.summary: The volunteer rescue network Hatzalah Judea and Samaria Without Borders listed 23 attacks on Israelis in Judea and Samaria on 9 and 10 October, which it said had largely gone unreported in the national media. They included stone-throwing near Or Yedidya that lightly injured a security officer, a vehicle set on fire by Arabs from Talfit, shepherds attacked or beaten near Ateret, Rachelim, al-Mughayyir and Osarin, and an attempt to seize a resident's weapon at the Kela David farm near Neve Tzuf. The booby-trapped PLO flag found on 9 October on Mount Hazor was destroyed in a controlled explosion on Saturday.
items.source: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria Without Borders

items.headline: Binyamin Brigade ends week-long operation; house of Netanel Shukron's murderer destroyed
items.summary: The IDF Binyamin Brigade and the Border Police of Judea and Samaria completed a week-long operation in five villages, searching more than 600 locations, seizing weapons and incitement material, and arresting wanted men, among them suspects in the transfer of terror funds. The forces destroyed the house of the Hamas operative from Biddu who murdered Netanel Shukron at the Ein Ria spring near Neve Tzuf before Yom Kippur. During the same week dozens of people who had expressed support for the massacre of 7 October were arrested across Judea and Samaria.

items.headline: Har Bracha widow asks the army to destroy the monument to her husband's murderer
items.summary: Lea Ziv-Parag, the widow of Yaakov Parag, who was murdered in December 1988 while guarding the lands of Har Bracha, has written to the head of Central Command, Major General Avi Bluth, asking the army to remove a monument to his murderer, Hamdan al-Najjar, which the family says stands near the place of the murder. The request follows the army's current campaign to remove monuments to terrorists in Judea and Samaria. MK Zvi Sukkot, chairman of the Knesset subcommittee on Judea and Samaria, joined the request and asked the IDF to act urgently.

items.headline: Eastern Binyamin: a sixteenth poisoning attack and two dummy bombs with PLO flags
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that infiltrators from al-Mughayyir again scattered poisoned dates on the grazing land of the Metzudat David farm during the night, and four goats died; he counted it as the sixteenth poisoning attack in the area of the Allon Road, and the Hatzalah volunteer network records 19 since the start of the year. On the same day the police announced that two dummy bombs with PLO flags attached had been found in Binyamin over the weekend, one near Mount Hazor and one near the Metzudat David farm. Elchanan Groner wrote that the placing of dummy bombs in eastern Binyamin has increased sharply in recent months, and that several real ones have already been found.

items.headline: Shin Bet arrests two settlement security officers in Samaria
items.summary: Arutz 7 reported that two security men living in Samaria, a community's military security coordinator and a security officer, were arrested at five in the morning on suspicion of involvement in violence against Palestinians near Aqraba about a month ago; they were barred from meeting a lawyer, and a gag order covers the case. The Petah Tikva Magistrate's Court extended their detention by four days, not the twelve days that the Shin Bet and the police had requested. The head of the Samaria Regional Council, Yossi Dagan, and the security coordinators of the Samaria Brigade protested against the manner of the arrests.

items.headline: Kafr Ana: the access road is blocked again, and no one is arrested
items.summary: Elisha Yered published video showing rioters from Ein Yabrud again blocking the access road to the Kafr Ana settlement point in Binyamin, under cover of the olive harvest, and reported that none of them was arrested. Kafr Ana stands on a hill between Ofra and Beit El and, according to Mr. Yered, connects the two communities. A public appeal raised 12,000 shekels within a day to pave a proper access road to the site before the winter.

items.headline: Kerem Binyamin farm: shepherd's finger broken; two attackers arrested in Burham
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that one of the shepherds attacked on Saturday near the Kerem Binyamin farm by Ateret went to hospital that night, where examinations found a broken finger and a probable sprain in the leg. The farm said that dozens of rioters took part and that no army or police force came to the site for almost a day. Later on 11 October IDF forces arrested two of the attackers in the village of Burham.

items.headline: Regavim: long-dead people are counted in Palestinian population censuses
items.summary: Regavim published an interview given to Channel 14 by Roi Drucker, its coordinator for Judea and Samaria, on the contradictory and unclear figures for the Palestinian population there. Regavim summarised the finding by saying that in the Palestinian Authority people who died long ago are counted in the censuses. The interview also explains why the true size of that population matters to Israel.

items.headline: High Court asks the state for a timetable for residents' return to the northern Samaria camps
items.summary: Olam Katan reported that Supreme Court President Yitzhak Amit and Justices Alex Stein and Khaled Kabub ordered the state to set out a timetable for the steps that would let residents return to the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps, and to examine whether those steps can be accelerated. The petition was filed by the Association for Civil Rights in Israel and six Palestinian petitioners. The IDF continues to operate in all three camps, and Olam Katan described the decision as judicial interference in the campaign against the terror centres of northern Samaria.

items.headline: Harvest orders: more land under IDF coordination, less closed to Israelis
items.summary: Peace Now reported that the head of Central Command has signed the harvest orders for 2026: Palestinians may enter about 88,300 dunams of olive groves only with prior coordination with the IDF, about 30 percent more than the 68,800 dunams of 2025 (a dunam is 1,000 square metres). The area closed to Israelis during the harvest has fallen from about 10,700 dunams in 2025 to 6,890 dunams this year. According to Peace Now, the coordination zones are drawn to protect new farms and hilltop communities and cover close to 20 percent of the olive groves in Judea and Samaria.
